Question: How does India’s Railways’ corporate train model work?
Old_Answer: Recently, IRCTC introduced Kashi Mahakal Express which is the country's third corporate train after two Tejas Exp trains between Delhi-Lucknow and Mumbai-Ahmedabad. All corporate trains are running with a new model which is actively pushed by Indian Railways to ' out source' the running of regular passenger trains. What is a Corporate Model? The Physical infrastructure of the train such as locomotives, coaches, locopilots among others will remain in Indisn Railway's hand. However, the services provided including ticketing and refunds, parcels, catering and housekeeping will be outsourced to the Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation and other such companies who will operate corporate trains in the future. Outsourcing the trains will help Indian Railways to earn a predecided fixed amount after every run based on three components and the owner of the network will be Indian Railways. Three components are: 1. Haulage : Operational amount paid to move a rake. For example: Track, Signalling, Locopilots and other physical involvement required to run a rake. IRCTC is paying INR 800/ Km to Railways for Lucknow Tejas. 2. Liese : Amount paid to Indian Railway Finance Corporation for the liece of coaches and locomotive. 3. Custody: Per day charges for the custody of rake which also includes maintainance cost which is around 2 lakh of one day in case of Lucknow Tejas. IRCTC is paying a sum total of 14 Lakh ( approx) per day ( up & down run) to the Indian Railways ( For Lucknow Tejas Express). • This is a fixed amount which IRCTC has to pay for every run, No matter train is running empty or full. IRCTC also shares a fixed profit precentage to the Railways. What are the powers that corporate entity will have? 1. As they are paying a heavy liece and custody amount to the railways so they have the suthority to select the rake and for sure every time a new rake will be asked for operation of any new train 2. IRCTC can change the service parameters itself without any approval from the ministry of railways. 3. Power of deciding the number of halts on decided route of any train. ☆The bright side for Indian Railways is that it doesn't have to suffer the losses in associated with running the trains. What is different between Private trains and corporate trains? Private trains are goods trains in which companies do not pay any liese and custody amount to the Railways. Question: Why do some train stations have only one passenger platform but has 2 railways? How does a train from the opposite side go to the other?
Old_Answer: India, being a massive country, has one of the largest railway networks in the world, which operates close to 28000 trains (passenger and freight) daily. There are almost 7400 railway stations in the Indian railway network to manage the smooth operations of the Indian Railways. The purpose of developing a railway station is not only to provide a platform for passengers but also to manage the massive traffic on Indian tracks. If we observe the network, we can find a railway station after every 4–8 km, and there is a reason behind that. Not all stations are purposely opened for passengers; some do not have a lot of foot fall, but they are very important for the railways. But why? So, the purpose of building a railway station after every 4–8 km and developing at least 2 railway tracks is to manage train operations properly. A second track is helpful in: i) Crossing: If two trains are supposed to cross each other, this scenario is common and useful on sections with single tracks. In that case, trains can only cross each other at these railway stations. Developing a raikway station after every 4–8 km helps in reducing the wait time for each train. ii) Overtake: If one train has to overtake the other train, in such senarios, railway stations play an important role in both single-line and double-line sections. iii) For idle rakes: Sometimes we find an empty rake at Railway Statiins. Generally, they are idled at slightly bigger stations so that the station is able to keep at least 2 tracks free for operations, but if necessary, small stations with 2 tracks use the loop line (second track) for idle rakes. iv) In case of technical failures or accidents: The second track always helps in these scenarios to park such trains and keep the main line clear for other trains. These were a few major benefits of having at least one extra track at railway stations. Mostly there is no second platform at railway stations is because of low footfall at that particular station, and in such cases, platform no. 1 is used for passenger trains so that people can easily board or deboard. Building a plstform and keeping operational requires a decent amount of money which railway avoids to spend if the foot fall at that railway station is low but a second track is important for the reasons I mentioned above. -Prashant Tiwari ✍️. Thank you for your valuable time.

Old_Answer: If you often book your train tickets online then you have surely seen an option named Auto Upgradation on the booking page. I'll try to go into detail about this feature and also discuss its purpose. What is auto upgradation? Auto upgradation is a complementary feature offered by railways to all its passengers, which upgrades their ticket to the higher class if seats are available after the first chart is prepared. How does it work? Suppose you have booked a confirmed train ticket in 3AC and opted for auto upgradation. Now at the time of charting the system checked and found that there is a waiting list in 3 AC but there are 3 seats available in 2AC. In that case, the system will upgrade your ticket to 2AC and vacate a berth for RAC passengers of 3AC and allot RAC to the waiting list passengers. Isn't that cool, right? How is it beneficial for Railways? We all know that online waiting list tickets get canceled after first charting i.e., 4 hours prior to the train's departure time and IRCTC initiates the refund in 1-3 working days. With this feature, the system upgrades a few tickets to higher class and make some seats available in the class where demand is high and allot those seats to RAC passengers whereas Waiting list passengers get RAC and now they can travel. This way Railways reduces the cancellations and of course some amount which they had to refund in case of cancellations.
